# duckalization

Content-addressed i18n for TypeScript/JavaScript. There are no translation
keys: the source-language text written in code IS the source of truth, and
every message's catalog ID is derived from its content.

Core invariant (frozen, shared by every package via `@duckalization/id`):

    id = base36( cyrb53( context ? context + "\u0000" + canonical(message)
                                 : canonical(message) ) )

- `canonical(string)` is the exact text — no trimming, no case folding,
  no whitespace collapsing. `"Sign in"` and `"Sign in "` are different messages.
- `canonical(pluralObject)` serializes forms in fixed CLDR order
  (zero, one, two, few, many, other) joined with `"\u0001"`, so property
  order in code never matters.
- Same text + same context → same ID, everywhere, forever. Editing the text
  intentionally produces a NEW ID: the old translation orphans itself and the
  new text shows up as untranslated. This replaces key-renaming rituals.

Packages (pnpm monorepo, all ESM, Node >= 20.19):

- `@duckalization/id`       — the hash. Frozen. Everything imports it.
- `@duckalization/extract`  — scans source (oxc parser), emits catalogs (library).
- `@duckalization/translate`— status diffing, translation briefs, validated apply,
                              glossary/style enforcement, review metadata (library).
- `@duckalization/cli`      — the `duckalize` bin: extract, translate, review commands.
- `@duckalization/runtime`  — client lookup/fallback/plurals/interpolation (~1.5kB gzip).
- `@duckalization/bundler-plugin` — optional unplugin; pre-bakes IDs at build time.
- `@duckalization/react`    — DuckProvider + useDuck()/useLocale() over runtime.

================================================================================
## 1. Writing translatable code (rules for authoring app code)
================================================================================

The extractor statically analyzes calls to `__(...)` (configurable names).
Every rule below is enforced by `duckalize extract` with a file:line error.

DO — these are the only four valid call shapes:

    __('Sign in')                                  // plain message
    __('Welcome back, {name}', { name })           // placeholders + values
    __('Book', { context: 'verb' })                // disambiguation
    __({ one: '{count} item', other: '{count} items' }, { count })  // plural

Options object semantics: it is ONE bag holding interpolation values plus two
reserved metadata keys, `context` and `id`. Reserved keys MUST be inline
string literals (the extractor must see them). Value entries may be any
expression.

    __('Checkout', { id: 'checkout.cta' })   // explicit ID override (escape hatch,
                                             // use only when a stable external ID is required)

DON'T — each of these is an extraction ERROR (build fails, nothing written):

    __(`Hello ${name}`)        // template-expressions: use '{name}' + values instead
    __(someVariable)           // dynamic-message: message must be a static literal
    __('')                     // empty-message
    __({ single: 'x' })        // invalid-plural: keys must be CLDR forms
    __({ one: 'x' })           // invalid-plural: 'other' form is required
    __('Hi', { context: v })   // invalid-meta: context/id must be inline literals

Details:
- Placeholder syntax is `{name}` (`[A-Za-z0-9_]+`). Never use JS template
  interpolation inside messages. Do not name a placeholder `context`, `id`,
  or (in non-plural messages) rely on `count` — those are reserved.
- Expressionless template literals are fine: __(`Sign in`) === __('Sign in').
- TS wrappers are unwrapped: `__({...} as const)` works.
- Plural messages: keys from {zero, one, two, few, many, other}; `other` is
  mandatory; every form must be a static string; pass `count` (number) in the
  options — it selects the form via Intl.PluralRules AND interpolates {count}.
- The same string in N places is ONE catalog entry (automatic dedup). If the
  same spelling has different meanings (noun/verb, screen A vs B), give the
  variants distinct `context` values — that is the ONLY correct fix for the
  `id-collision` error, and for translation-differs-by-meaning situations.
- Only bare-identifier calls are matched. `i18n.__('x')` is NOT extracted.
  Keep `__` a plain imported/destructured binding.
- To fix a typo or reword: just edit the string. The ID changes, the old
  entry orphans, retranslation happens on the next translate pass. Never add
  `_v2`-style suffixes.

================================================================================
## 2. Extraction: CLI, config, outputs
================================================================================

    duckalize extract              # writes <outDir>/<sourceLocale>.json + .meta.json
    duckalize extract --dry-run    # report only
    Flags: --cwd <path> --config <path> --out-dir <path> --silent

Exit code 1 and NO files written if any diagnostic is an error (all
extraction diagnostics are errors; the codes are: parse-error,
dynamic-message, template-expressions, empty-message, invalid-plural,
invalid-meta, id-collision).

Optional `duckalization.config.json` at project root (all fields optional):

    {
      "include": ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mts,mjs,cts,cjs}"],   // default
      "exclude": ["**/node_modules/**", "**/dist/**", "**/*.d.ts",
                  "**/*.test.*", "**/*.spec.*"],                  // default
      "functions": ["__"],                                        // default
      "outDir": "locales",                                        // default
      "sourceLocale": "en",                                       // default
      "targetLocales": ["es", "pt"],                              // for translate
      "style": {                                                  // tone guides, per locale
        "*":  "UI copy: concise, sentence case.",                 // '*' = all locales
        "es": "./locales/style/es.md"                             // inline text or .md path
      },
      "glossary": "locales/glossary.json"                         // default
    }

Outputs (keys sorted, deterministic — diffs are meaningful):

    locales/en.json        — flat catalog: { "<id>": "text" | {one,other,...} }
    locales/en.meta.json   — sidecar per id:
                             { "message": ..., "context"?: "...",
                               "refs": ["src/File.tsx:12:5", ...] }

Programmatic API (`@duckalization/extract`):

    import { extract, writeOutputs } from '@duckalization/extract';
    const result = await extract({ cwd });   // pure: reads sources, writes nothing
    // result: { catalog, meta, diagnostics, stats, config }
    if (!result.diagnostics.some(d => d.severity === 'error'))
      await writeOutputs(result, result.config);

================================================================================
## 3. Runtime (`@duckalization/runtime`)
================================================================================

    import { createDuck } from '@duckalization/runtime';

    const duck = createDuck({
      sourceLocale: 'en',        // default 'en' — locale of the inline strings
      locale: 'en',              // default sourceLocale
      onMissing: (id, message, locale) => {},  // or false; default warns once
    });                                        // per entry outside production

    export const { __ } = duck;   // bound; destructuring is safe and is the
                                  // extractable calling pattern

    duck.load('es', catalogObject);  // merge; repeated calls accumulate chunks
    duck.setLocale('es');
    duck.getLocale();
    duck.subscribe(fn);              // () => unsubscribe; fires on load/setLocale
    duck.getVersion();               // monotonic counter for useSyncExternalStore

Behavior of `__(message, options?, injectedId?)`:
- Active locale === sourceLocale → returns the inline text (interpolated).
  No hashing, no lookup. Untranslated apps pay ~nothing.
- Otherwise resolves ID (injectedId → options.id → memoized hash), looks up
  the catalog for the exact locale, then the base language ('es-MX' → 'es').
  Miss → onMissing fires and the inline source text is returned. Rendering
  never throws over a missing translation.
- Plural form selection uses `Intl.PluralRules(locale)`. Translated plural
  entries MAY carry forms the source lacks (Russian few/many) — the runtime
  picks whatever the locale's rules select, falling back to `other`.
- `injectedId` (3rd arg) is written ONLY by the bundler plugin. Never write
  it by hand; humans/agents use `{ id }` in options.
- SSR: create one duck per request. Never share a mutable instance across
  concurrently rendered locales.
- TypeScript checks placeholders at compile time: `__('Hi {name}')` without a
  `name` value is a type error. If you see that error, add the value — do not
  restructure the message to dodge the type.

================================================================================
## 4. Bundler plugin (`@duckalization/bundler-plugin`) — optional
================================================================================

Rewrites at build time so the runtime never hashes (hash tree-shakes out):

    __('Sign in')            →  __('Sign in', undefined, "28ki3q224lm")
    __('msg', { name })      →  __('msg', { name }, "<id>")

    // vite.config.ts
    import DuckalizationPlugin from '@duckalization/bundler-plugin';
    plugins: [DuckalizationPlugin.vite()]     // .rollup() .webpack() .esbuild()

    Options: { functions?: string[]; include?: RegExp; exclude?: RegExp;
               failOnError?: boolean /* default false: warn */ }

Idempotent (3-arg calls skipped). Apps behave identically without the plugin —
it is a performance optimization, never a correctness requirement.

================================================================================
## 5. React (`@duckalization/react`)
================================================================================

Re-exports `createDuck`; a React app needs only this package.

    // i18n.ts (module scope client-side; per-request on the server)
    import { createDuck } from '@duckalization/react';
    export const duck = createDuck({ sourceLocale: 'en' });

    // root
    <DuckProvider duck={duck}><App /></DuckProvider>

    // components
    const { __ } = useDuck();          // subscribed: re-renders on setLocale/load
    const [locale, setLocale] = useLocale();
    return <h1>{__('Sign in')}</h1>;

`useDuck()` throws outside a provider. Rich text is out of scope by design:
messages are plain strings; render markdown/formatting around them.

================================================================================
## 6. The translation workflow (`duckalize translate` / `duckalize review`)
================================================================================

    duckalize translate status            # per-locale: translated/missing/orphaned
    duckalize translate check             # CI gate: exit 1 if anything is missing
    duckalize translate brief [locale…]   # work orders → locales/.work/<locale>.brief.json
    duckalize translate apply <file…>     # validate agent output, merge, record review meta
    duckalize translate prune [locale…]   # archive+remove orphaned ids
    duckalize translate lint [locale…]    # run the apply-time checks on existing catalogs
    duckalize review status [locale…]     # approved/machine/edited/unreviewed counts
    duckalize review approve <locale> [--id <id>…] [--by <name>]

The loop: `brief` → an agent translates the brief → `apply`. The brief is
SELF-CONTAINED (entries + context + call-site source excerpts + glossary
subset + style guide + the locale's real CLDR plural categories) — the
translating agent needs no repo access.

### Translating a brief (instructions for a translation agent)

Follow the brief's embedded `instructions`. Respond with ONLY:

    { "locale": "es",
      "translations": { "<id>": "…" | { "one": "…", "other": "…" }, … },
      "notes": { "<id>": { "confidence": "low|medium|high",
                            "alternatives": ["…"], "note": "…" } } }

1. Copy IDs verbatim. Never invent, rename, or drop one.
2. String entries stay strings; plural entries stay objects.
3. Preserve `{placeholder}` tokens exactly; reorder freely for grammar.
4. Plural entries: produce the forms the brief's `pluralCategories` lists;
   `other` is always required. More or fewer forms than the source is fine.
5. Glossary: `doNotTranslate` terms must appear verbatim (validated as a hard
   error at apply time); prefer `approvedTranslation` where given (validated
   as a warning); `note` explains the product meaning.
6. Follow the `style` guide for tone, register, and dialect.
7. `notes` are optional but recorded in review metadata — include confidence.

### What apply validates (errors reject the whole file; nothing is written)

errors:   unknown-id, type-mismatch, empty-translation, missing-other,
          invalid-plural-form, unknown-placeholder (typo'd {token}),
          glossary-dnt (brand term was translated)
warnings: missing-placeholder (dropped token — sometimes legitimate),
          unexpected-plural-form (form this locale never selects),
          glossary-term (approved translation not used), orphaned-id (lint)

### Glossary (`locales/glossary.json`)

    { "Soundbite":  { "translate": false, "note": "Product feature name" },
      "assignment": { "note": "A homework unit a teacher assigns",
                      "translations": { "es": "tarea", "pt": "tarefa" } } }

### Review metadata (`locales/<locale>.review.json`, committed)

Written by `apply` (status "machine", content hash, by/at, agent notes).
`review status` derives effective state: hash drift = hand-edited ("edited");
`review approve` records sign-off. Review state is keyed by content-derived
ID, so it self-invalidates when the English text changes. Catalog diffs are
deterministic — a git PR is the intended review surface.

Orphans: an ID in a target catalog but not the source is stale; `prune`
archives it to `locales/.archive/<locale>.json` before removal. A partial
catalog is always safe to ship: missing IDs render the inline source text.

================================================================================
## 7. Using it today (monorepo not yet on npm)
================================================================================

From a sibling project, reference the built packages with the file: protocol
(pnpm symlinks and resolves workspace deps transitively):

    cd /path/to/duckalization && pnpm install && pnpm build
    # in the consuming app:
    pnpm add /path/to/duckalization/packages/runtime \
             /path/to/duckalization/packages/react
    pnpm add -D /path/to/duckalization/packages/cli \
                /path/to/duckalization/packages/bundler-plugin

Minimal wiring checklist for a new app:
1. `pnpm add` runtime (or react) as above; cli as a dev dependency.
2. Create `src/i18n.ts`: `createDuck()`, export `{ __ }` (and the duck).
3. Write UI text via the four valid call shapes (section 1).
4. Config: set `targetLocales`, write `locales/glossary.json` and per-locale
   `style` guides (section 2 / section 6).
5. `duckalize extract` → commit `locales/en.json` + `locales/en.meta.json`.
6. `duckalize translate brief` → translate the brief (section 6) →
   `duckalize translate apply <output.json> --by <agent-name>`.
7. `duck.load('es', esCatalog)` (static import or lazy) + `setLocale`.
8. Review: `duckalize review status` / `approve`; gate CI with
   `duckalize translate check`.
9. Optional: add the bundler plugin (section 4).

Invariants to never violate:
- Do not modify `@duckalization/id`'s canonicalization or hash.
- Do not hand-edit generated catalogs of the source locale; re-run extract.
- Do not write the 3rd `__()` argument by hand.
- Keep `__` a bare identifier; do not wrap it in a namespace or method.
